note: Recurring demand PERIODS, as opposed to the dated points Calendarific supplies. This file exists because a calendar API only knows discrete festivals, yet the biggest demand drivers in Indian retail are spans: wedding season runs November to February and moves more ethnic wear than any single festival. Without these, a bridal saree with 1.4 days of stock raises no warning because no dated event is tagged `wedding`. Dates are MM-DD and recur every year; a span whose end month is earlier than its start month wraps across the new year. Hand-curated deliberately - there is no free API for this, and the list is small and stable enough that curation beats inference.

seasons.name: Wedding season (North India)
seasons.description: The main Hindu wedding muhurat window. Drives bridal and wedding-guest wear, jewellery and gifting harder than any single festival.

seasons.name: Wedding season (South India)
seasons.description: Southern auspicious wedding window, distinct from the northern one. Silk sarees, temple jewellery.

seasons.name: Summer
seasons.description: Hot season. Shifts demand toward cottons, linens, light colours and away from silks and heavy work.

seasons.name: Monsoon
seasons.description: Rain season. Quick-dry and synthetic fabrics, waterproof footwear; suppresses demand for delicate and heavy garments.

seasons.name: Winter
seasons.description: Cold season in the north. Shawls, stoles, woollens, layering pieces.

seasons.name: Festive season
seasons.description: The long festive run from Onam through Navratri, Durga Puja and Dussehra to Diwali. The single largest retail window of the Indian year.

seasons.name: Back to school
seasons.description: School reopening across most Indian boards. Uniforms, bags, footwear, stationery.
